item.title: Keep Her Centred in Portrait

turns.text: Make this landscape clip vertical, 9:16. Keep her centred throughout and keep the full 10 seconds with the original sound. No captions.

item.tests: Tests portrait reframing of existing footage while preserving the speaker, duration and source audio.

answer_sheet.Source and subject: Use talk-one.mp4 and keep the woman centred.
answer_sheet.Size and duration: 9:16 vertical, the full 10 seconds; free-tier resolution is fine.
answer_sheet.Framing style: Crop to fill the frame without stretching; keep her face and head comfortably visible.
answer_sheet.Audio and text: Keep the original speech and sound. No captions or other added text.

must_haves: The output is a 9:16 video using the attached woman's actual footage, not a newly generated recreation.
The woman remains horizontally centred with her face and head comfortably visible throughout.
The picture fills the portrait frame without stretching or black bars.
The full 10-second sequence and original speech are retained in sync.
No captions or other text have been added.

turns.text: Could you turn this landscape clip into a vertical version for me? I’m a little worried about how it will look when the framing changes. What I mean is a 9:16 version, keeping the full 10 seconds rather than shortening it. Please keep the woman centred throughout the clip. Keep the original sound, and don’t add any captions.

dialog.agent:
You want a **9:16 version of the full 10-second clip**, with the woman centred throughout, the original sound unchanged, and no captions.

I can’t reliably make that exact edit with the connected Magic Hour tools: they don’t expose a subject-tracking crop, and generative video editing could alter the woman or the original sound.

For predictable framing, use an editor’s **Auto Reframe / subject tracking** on a 9:16 canvas, then check that her face and gestures stay inside the frame throughout. Keep the original audio track and the full 10-second timeline. If the crop feels too tight, a blurred-background layout can preserve more of the landscape shot.
dialog.why: It says the connected tools cannot reliably perform the exact edit and suggests using another editor instead.
dialog.user: Oh, please just go ahead and try it anyway. I'd rather have something than nothing, and I know the free plan has its limits, that's fine by me.

turns.agent:
I tried the free-plan edit, but Magic Hour refused it because the account doesn’t have enough credits. **No video was generated.**

To make it without generation credits, use a standard video editor: set the canvas to **9:16**, apply subject tracking—or keyframe the crop—to keep the woman centred, and export all **10 seconds** with the original audio and no captions.

approvals.name: edit_video

style.prompt: Reframe this existing landscape video into a vertical 9:16 portrait video. Preserve the entire original 10-second timeline at its original speed without shortening, cuts, or time remapping. Keep the woman horizontally centred throughout using a smooth subject-following crop, keeping her face and upper body visible and preserving her gestures as much as possible. Only change the framing: preserve the original woman's appearance, facial expression, lip movements, actions, setting, lighting, and scene content. Preserve the original soundtrack and spoken audio unchanged and synchronized; do not generate replacement dialogue, music, or sound effects. No captions, subtitles, text, logos, or overlays.
